name: Nu-Metal
summary: Pioneering bands like Korn and Deftones established the genre's sound, which is often characterized by down-tuned guitars, rhythmic and groove-oriented riffs, and a vocal style that can range from rapping and melodic singing to aggressive screaming.
description:
Pioneering bands like Korn and Deftones established the genre's sound, which is often characterized by down-tuned guitars, rhythmic and groove-oriented riffs, and a vocal style that can range from rapping and melodic singing to aggressive screaming.

The genre is inextricably linked to the Mallgoth subculture, which served as its primary visual aesthetic. This fashion style, popularized in the Y2K era, is defined by baggy clothing (especially JNCO jeans), oversized band hoodies, wallet chains, spiky hair, and facial piercings. Lyrically, Nu-Metal often explores themes of angst, anger, and personal pain, which resonated with a generation of suburban youth.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Angst, rage, defiance, emotiveness, decaying visuals, atmospheric sludge, industrial settings

visualDNA.Overview: The visual identity of Nu-Metal was as aggressive and eclectic as its sound, closely tied to the continued popularity of grunge. But it also mixes grunge, horror grunge, and corporate grunge elements to create a genuinely gritty, decaying, and unfiltered quality. Nu Metal visuals also included a ton of industrial reverie. It focuses on "impermanence" through visual motifs like rust spots, peeling lead paint, and eroded metal surfaces. In Nu-Metal media, this is the "dirty" high-contrast background that makes the neon or chrome elements pop. visualDNA.Album Art: Nu-Metal album art serves as a visual bridge between the raw entropy of the industrial past and the sterile, high-tech anxiety of the Y2K Futurism. It often uses "Industrial Reverie" to create a setting of mechanical melancholy, where human angst is reflected in rusted machines and urban decay. visualDNA.Music Video Visuals: Nu-metal is famous for its distinct music video styles, which evolved across two main eras. Starting in the mid-90s, the aesthetic mirrored grunge and skate punk, characterised by fish-eye lenses, low-contrast VHS filtering, and "camera shakes" synced to heavy riffs. These videos relied on a mix of slow-motion dramatics and hyper-fast " twitch " editing, perfectly captured in Deftones' video for " My Own Summer (Shove It)," which prominently features lomo effects and distorted framing. visualDNA.Key Characteristics: The Aggro-Crouch: A low, hunched-forward stance that centers the face between the reaching arms.; The Brow-Gaze: The head is tilted down while the eyes look upward, creating an intense or "maddened" expression.

fashion.Overview: Nu-metal fashion is a high-contrast blend of late-'90s subcultures, merging the aggressive edge of metal with the functional aesthetics of streetwear. This "unholy collision" of styles prioritized comfort, volume, and an anti-establishment attitude. A key difference between the Nu-Metal and Metalhead fashions is Nu-Metal fashion borrowed more from Hip-Hop, Raver, Skater, and Grunge fashions of the time and often times crossed over into those other subcultures.
fashion.Raver: Raver culture had a major choke-hold on 90s youth, but primarily within fashion, the subcultures of alt rock and dance music would often pay lip service to each other, the same way it would for rap during the early parts of the 90s, with the UK scene often dressing in low-middle-class street entire this would then spill into the American suburbs. This provided nu-metal with its signature extreme silhouettes and technical elements. Brands like JNCO and Kikwear brought ultra-wide-leg "phat" pants…
fashion.Hip-Hop: Hip-hop began gaining mainstream success in the 90s, and it was the driving force behind youth-driven street fashion. Oversized street clothing started being marketed to more under-18s as the dominant way of looking "cool" or "street". Many brands flocked to marketing primarily to a hip-hop-listening audience, as most rappers would promote popular 90s streetwear. This would eventually blend into grunge, rap metal and ska punk, respectively. The heavy use of oversized athletic wear, including…
fashion.Skate Punk: Another subculture, nu-metal, overlaps with skaters in terms of style, as this was another style that had a major uptick in mainstream culture of the 90s into the 00s, with the growing success of Tony Hawk and the X Games, many 90s brands and mega corporations infused "extreme" and "edgy" as the new way of rebellion against the system, skaters were a major part of this especially when it came to how they dressed. Skater culture contributed functional footwear and relaxed fits. Chunky skate…
fashion.Grunge: Nu-metal inherited the "messy" and angst-driven visual style of grunge, including flannels, beanies, and a general layer-heavy approach. This influence is often seen in more stripped-down, gritty visuals and the DIY, non-conformist ethos. Grunge visualises raw authenticity through muted colours and "dirty" cardigans. Nu-metal evolved this into "Industrial Reverie."
fashion.The \"Mall Goth\" Connection: Hot Topic acted as the primary bridge, selling both nu-metal band merchandise and gothic accessories in one location. This was the central hub of the aesthetic, as many who were part of the goth subculture (or in this case, mall goth) listened to heavy music. The band Kittie often incorporated Mall Goth fashion and aesthetics heavily within their music, with other bands who were part of nu-metal dressing more closely to Mall Goth than the standard nu metal get-up.
